memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull's blood and carry it into the tent of meeting. He is to dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary."'" - Lev 4:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something new happens here. In the burnt offering and the fellowship offering, the blood stayed outside on the altar. Now, for the first time, blood is carried inside the tent.

Sin does more damage than we think. It does not simply create a problem between me and my neighbour, or even a problem in my own conscience. It reaches inward, toward the holy place, toward God Himself. So the blood must go where the damage went.

Seven times before the curtain — the number of completeness. Nothing partial. Nothing half-covered.

And yet notice where the priest stops. In front of the curtain. He sprinkles toward the Most Holy Place but he does not enter it. Not on this day. The curtain still hangs, and it says: not yet, not fully, not for anyone.

Hebrews explains that the Holy Spirit was showing by this that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed (Heb 9:8). The whole system was honest about its own limits.

Then Matthew records what happened at the moment Jesus died: the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom (Mtt 27:51). Torn from the top — God's hand, not ours. What Aaron could only sprinkle toward, Christ walked through.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I grasp how deeply sin reaches, beyond just its visible consequences?
2. What does it mean to me that the curtain is torn and the way is open?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, my sin reached further than I knew, and Christ's blood reached further still. Thank You that the curtain is torn and I may come in. Amen.
